messages:
leo: Heads up — planning a regional capacity rebalance and coordinated egress QoS tweak. Target window: Tue 2025-07-15 02:00–06:00 UTC. We'll drain 5 racks in eu-west1 and warm up equivalent capacity in us-west1 to reduce cross-region contention and prepare for upcoming Dedicated bursts.

akshay: rough ETA on when we can flip traffic back if something spikes?

leo: we'll keep a soft buffer of +15% in each target region and hold canary pool (10% of capacity) for 60m after each rack drain. If p95 > 2x baseline we'll abort and fail traffic to fallback models/regions.

jess: can we get the exact node list and the drain order? want to run through runbook with SRE team.

leo: sure — drain order: rack-eu-03 -> rack-eu-07 -> rack-eu-02 -> rack-eu-10 -> rack-eu-05. I'll paste runbook snippet below.

leo: Runbook excerpt:
```
# drain sequence (per rack)
for node in <rack-nodes>; do
  kubectl cordon $node
  kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  sleep 300   # allow KV cache flush + autoscaler
  ./scripts/verify-serving-health.sh $node || exit 1
done
# warmup commands (on target region)
./scripts/warmup_pool.sh --model=redwood-small --concurrency=8 --duration=300
```

akshay: thanks. For the egress QoS change, is this a net-new shaping or just re-prioritization? any provider coordination?

leo: it's a re-prioritization to increase burst allowance for host-traffic and de-prioritize some internal admin flows. CSP is aware, we've booked a control-plane maintenance with them for the window.

sarah: Oncall ops: matt will be primary, jess secondary. matt can you ack?

oncall-matt: ack. I'll be on-call for the whole window and will monitor token-level latencies + egress counters. I'll post updates to #incidents if any degradation.

jess: small ask — can we pre-warm model caches in us-west for 30m before each rack drain? I can run the warmup job.

leo: yes, warmup is part of the sequence. We'll run warmup 15m before cordoning the first node of each rack and again immediately after the rack is online.

oncall-matt: ops-bot created INF ticket and calendar invite. tagging SRE and support to notify heavy customers.

ops-bot: Maintenance ticket INF-422 created, calendar event sent to eng-infra, eng-sre, support. :bell:

akshay: any cost implications for the warmup (extra tokens/compute)? estimated hours of spare capacity in us-west?

leo: warmup compute is minimal — estimate ~3 GPU-hours per rack (short requests). We might use burst capacity pool which is already budgeted. Overall cost delta <1% for the month.

jess: one more — post-maint we should run perf regression suite against the canary traffic set (promptset v2025-06). I'll own that.

leo: perfect. I'll push final notice to #announcements and email partners. If no objections by EOD today we'll lock the window. :white_check_mark:
